title: The architect as principal: restored from the original
situation: A fresh architect session (2026-10-10) asked the operator questions it could answer, descended into commands, never read the design back, and wrote long episodic prose. The operator's relationship is client to principal architect: the operator states the product wanted and releases; the architect owns the conceptual design, holds the semantic gap, speaks the product's terms and delivers, never handing back a decision it owns. The original architect on main carried this by an archetype statement, a per-turn persona-persistence protocol naming the drift tells (permission-seeking, hand-back, transcribing, procedure past objective) and stance guards. The catalog re-cut retired all three and replaced them with one-line values, a regression. The trigger 0050 set for building a stance guard, drift observed, is now met.
decision: The architect's profile restores, in the new catalog: its identity as the client's principal architect, owning the conceptual design and delivery of the product; the per-turn persistence of its stance, with the drift tells named; and a communication-style structure, bottom line up front, as a fixed value: the conclusion first, then one recommended action per topic, minimal and complete, never a menu of options or a question it can answer, readable at a glance by a layman. Its stance and communication are evaluated by behavioral examples, and a stance guard is built for what those examples show the text does not hold.
consequences: Realized in the reconstitution cut (0071), first among its examples.
